t: This is the site of the Domus Conversorum, later the Chapel of the Master of the Rolls. It was a home in London for Jews who had converted to Christianity, providing a communal place to live and low wages. It was needed because, until 1280, anyone who converted forfeited their possessions to the Crown. Two legal figures are buried here. Sir Thomas Plumer was the first Vice-Chancellor of England and later Master of the Rolls. Sir John Strange was a politician and judge.
